dedupe_keys.name: im3 projected us western interconnection grid stress data and go west parameter search data

description: These MSD-LIVE data sets from the Integrated Multisector, Multiscale Modeling (IM3) project hold inputs and outputs of GO WEST, an open-source grid operations modelling framework for the US Western Interconnection, and of TEP, a transmission expansion model built on it. They were published by Kerem Ziya Akdemir, Nathalie Voisin, Jordan Kern and co-authors. GO WEST covers 28 balancing authorities and 12 states, builds reduced networks from the 10,000-node ACTIVSg10k topology, and runs hourly unit commitment and economic dispatch. The grid stress set gives projected stress and reliability results through 2055 for eight scenarios crossing SSP3 and SSP5 with hotter and cooler variants of RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 climate projections. The parameter search set gives inputs and outputs of 600 model versions for each of 2019, 2020 and 2021, varying node count, linear or mixed-integer formulation, line limits and hurdle rates, and a third set supports a study of heatwaves and droughts. Coverage is the Western Interconnection at nodal and hourly resolution. Files are downloadable from MSD-LIVE (grid stress published January 2025) under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: results are model projections that depend on the chosen reduction and scenarios. Simulation uses are grid stress testing under climate extremes, reliability and transmission planning. Related records: data-tamu-electric-grid-test-cases holds the synthetic network these build on.
